([[Sydney]], Australia) | college = [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico]] (2017–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = 2021–2022 | team1 = [[Kouvot]] | years2 = 2022–2024 | team2 = [[Darwin Salties]] | years3 = 2022–2023 | team3 = [[Melbourne United]] | years4 = 2023–present | team4 = [[Sydney Kings]] | years5 = 2025 | team5 = Mackay Meteors | highlights = * [[List of NBL champions|NBL champion]] (2026) * Third-team All-[[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] (2021) }} '''Makuach Maker Maluach''' (born 4 May 1998) is an Australian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sydney Kings]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He played [[college basketball]] in the United States for the [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico Lobos]] from 2017 to 2021. Maluach started his professional career in Finland with [[Kouvot]] during the 2021–22 season. He began his NBL career with [[Melbourne United]] in 2022 and joined the Kings the following season. Maluach won an [[List of NBL champions|NBL championship]] with the Kings in 2026. ==Early life== Maluach was born in Uganda as the fourth of six brothers.{{cite web |title=Melbourne United Multicultural Stories: Makuach Maluach |url=https://www.melbourneutd.com.au/news/melbourne-united-multicultural-stories-makuach-maluach |website=Melbourne United |access-date=30 May 2026 |date=4 November 2022}} He is of South Sudanese descent. Maluach and his family moved to [[Armidale]], Australia, in 2009 as refugees.{{cite web |last1=Dunger |first1=Ellen |title=Makuach Maluach is set to play college basketball in the US |url=https://www.northerndailyleader.com.au/story/4828428/from-refugee-to-us-basketball-spotlight/ |website=The Northern Daily Leader |access-date=30 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171112091701/https://www.northerndailyleader.com.au/story/4828428/from-refugee-to-us-basketball-spotlight/ |archive-date=12 November 2017 |date=2 August 2017}} He started playing basketball the following year when he was aged 12. Maluach attended [[Newington College]] in [[Sydney]]. ==College basketball career== Maluach received a scholarship to play [[college basketball]] in the United States for the [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico Lobos]] in 2017. He was selected to the All-[[Mountain West Conference]] third-team as a senior in 2021.{{cite web |title=Maluach Named to All-Mountain West Third Team |url=https://golobos.com/news/2021/03/9/maluach-named-to-all-mountain-west-third-team |website=The University of New Mexico |access-date=30 May 2026 |date=9 March 2021}} Maluach was eligible for a fifth year but decided to begin his professional career and sign with an agent.{{cite web |last1=Chester |first1=Jared |title=Makuach Maluach will miss the Lobos but excited to start pro career |url=https://www.krqe.com/sports/local-sports/makuach-maluach-will-miss-the-lobos-but-excited-to-start-pro-career/ |website=KRQE |access-date=30 May 2026 |date=23 May 2021}} He declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] but was not selected.{{cite web |title=Makuach Maluach 2021 Senior Underclassmen |url=https://www.thedraftreview.com/honorable-draftees?view=article&id=12926:makuach-maluach&catid=141 |website=The Draft Review |access-date=30 May 2026}} ==Professional career== On 27 August 2021, Maluach signed with [[Kouvot]] of the [[Korisliiga]] in Finland.{{cite web |title=Kouvojen rosteri vahvistuu jälleen: Makuach Maluach mukaan Kouvolan huippukorikseen! |url=https://kouvot.fi/2021/08/kouvojen-rosteri-vahvistuu-jalleen-makuach-maluach-mukaan-kouvolan-huippukorikseen/ |website=Kouvot |access-date=30 May 2026 |language=Finnish |date=27 August 2021}} He averaged 13.6 points and 5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Melbourne Sign Makuach Maluach |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/melbourne-sign-makuach-maluach |website=NBL |access-date=30 May 2026 |date=20 May 2022}} Maluach played for the [[Darwin Salties]] of the [[NBL1 North]] in 2022. He gained attention for a poster dunk he made in a game against the RedCity Roar.{{cite web |last1=Sullivan |first1=Matthew |title=‘Oh my god’: Australian basketball fans stunned by ‘dunk of the year’ |url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/basketball/oh-my-god-australian-basketball-fans-stunned-by-dunk-of-the-year/news-story/21a2b5443c09dafc0bd088efe1db276a |website=news.com.au |access-date=30 May 2026 |date=1 May 2022}} On 20 May 2022, Maluach signed a one-year contract with [[Melbourne United]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). Maluach returned to the Salties for the 2023 NBL1 North season and averaged 22.5 points, 8.6 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Darwin Salties re-sign star player |url=https://www.nbl1.com.au/news/darwin-salties-re-sign-star-player |website=NBL1 |access-date=30 May 2026 |date=30 January 2024}} On 12 April 2023, Maluach signed a two-year contract with the [[Sydney Kings]] of the NBL.{{cite web |title=Kings add explosive Maluach to NBL24 roster |url=https://www.sydneykings.com/news/kings-add-explosive-maluach-to-nbl24-roster |website=Sydney Kings |access-date=30 May 2026 |date=12 April 2023}} On 30 January 2024, Maluach re-signed with the Salties for the 2024 NBL1 North season. On 22 April 2025, Maluach signed with the Mackay Meteors for the NBL1 North season.{{cite web |title=🚨 𝐍𝐁𝐋𝟏 𝐏𝐋𝐀𝐘𝐄𝐑 𝐀𝐍𝐍𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐂𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐍𝐓 🚨 |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DIu6WXkp3lu/ |website=Instagram |publisher=Mackay Basketball |access-date=30 May 2026 |date=22 April 2025}} On 28 April 2025, Maluach re-signed with the Kings on a one-year deal.{{cite web |title=Kings re-sign NSW product Makuach Maluach |url=https://www.sydneykings.com/news/kings-re-sign-nsw-product-makuach-maluach |website=Sydney Kings |access-date=30 May 2026 |date=28 April 2025}} He had a breakout year during the 2025–26 season when he averaged an NBL career-best 8.4 points and 3.1 rebounds per game which earned him a nomination for the [[NBL Most Improved Player Award]].{{cite web |title=NBL champion re-signs in Sydney |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/nbl-champion-makuach-maluach-re-signs-in-sydney |website=NBL |access-date=30 May 2026 |date=29 April 2026}} The Kings won the [[List of NBL champions|NBL championship]] in 2026. On 29 April 2026, Maluach re-signed with the Kings on a two-year deal. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://www.nbl.com.au/players/makuach-maluach Makuach Maluach] at [[National Basketball League (Australia)|NBL]] *[https://www.nbl1.com.au/player-listing/makuach-maluach-9c2da2b3-c6f1-11ec-be3c-d9a2f7c521e6 Makuach Maluach] at [[NBL1]] *[https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/229098-makuach-maker-maluach Makuach Maluach] at [[FIBA]] *[https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/190947/makuach-maluach Makuach Maluach] at Proballers *[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/makuach-maluach-1.html Makuach Maluach college stats] at [[Sports Reference]] *[https://golobos.com/sports/mbball/roster/player/makuach-maluach New Mexico Lobos bio] {{Sydney Kings current roster}} {{Sydney Kings 2025–26 NBL champions}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Maluach, Makuach}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Australian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Australian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Australian people of South Sudanese descent]] [[Category:Basketball players from Sydney]] [[Category:Guards (basketball)]] [[Category:Kouvot players]] [[Category:Melbourne United players]] [[Category:New Mexico Lobos men's basketball players]] [[Category:People educated at Newington College]] [[Category:Sydney Kings players]]
